section_summary: This section concerns Japanese taxation during the Allied occupation, especially exemptions from the capital levy and other extraordinary taxes for United Nations nationals, Koreans, Formosans and Swiss nationals. Correspondence records Far Eastern Commission policy, disputes over its application, and a decision to delay publicity until Japan’s tax bills passed. The final pages contain a 1948 report on Japanese tax reform, delinquent payments, corporate tax arrears and collection difficulties; part of that report is duplicated and continues beyond page 68.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference note on proposed Japanese tax law
subfiles.about: Points to a report from Switzerland on a proposed Japanese tax law.
subfiles.summary: References a January 16, 1945 report filed elsewhere.

subfiles.title: Memorandum for the Secretary: directive regarding Japanese taxation of aliens
subfiles.about: Requests transmission of a Far Eastern Commission tax directive to General MacArthur.
subfiles.summary: Seeks Joint Chiefs of Staff review and transmission of the directive, with notice that further policy on war-related extraordinary taxes remains under consideration.

subfiles.title: Statement of policy regarding Japanese taxation of aliens
subfiles.about: Sets out nondiscrimination and capital levy exemptions for United Nations nationals.
subfiles.summary: Bars discriminatory taxation and generally exempts United Nations nationals’ property and corporate interests from capital levies.

subfiles.title: Directive regarding Japanese taxation of aliens
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Directs occupation authorities to ensure Japanese tax laws follow Far Eastern Commission policy.
subfiles.summary: Instructs the Supreme Commander to enforce nondiscrimination and capital levy exemptions, referring exceptional cases to the Commission.

subfiles.title: Certification of Far Eastern Commission decision
subfiles.about: Certifies the attached July 18 policy decision as a correct copy.
subfiles.summary: Certifies the copy of the Commission’s unanimously adopted decision.

subfiles.title: Japanese taxation of aliens
subfiles.about: States the Commission’s rules for taxation of aliens and capital levies.
subfiles.summary: Prohibits discriminatory taxes and exempts United Nations nationals’ property from capital levies.

subfiles.title: Letter forwarding Japanese taxation policy
subfiles.about: Forwards the Far Eastern Commission decision for preparation of a directive.
subfiles.summary: Johnson forwards the unanimous policy decision and asks that MacArthur also be told the Commission is considering other extraordinary war-cost taxes.

subfiles.title: Memorandum for the Secretary: directive regarding Japanese taxation of aliens
subfiles.about: Repeats the request to transmit the tax directive and accompanying policy.
subfiles.summary: Requests Joint Chiefs of Staff transmission and notice of further Commission work on war-related taxes.

subfiles.title: Directive regarding Japanese taxation of aliens
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Repeats instructions implementing the Far Eastern Commission’s alien-tax policy.
subfiles.summary: Requires Japanese tax laws to follow nondiscrimination and capital levy exemption principles.

subfiles.title: Statement of policy regarding Japanese taxation of aliens
subfiles.about: Repeats the Commission’s policy on aliens and capital levies.
subfiles.summary: Bars discriminatory taxation and generally exempts United Nations nationals from capital levies.

subfiles.title: Conversation on exemption from Japanese extraordinary taxes
subfiles.about: Records discussion of the United States position on exemptions from three Japanese taxes.
subfiles.summary: Participants discuss whether United Nations nationals should pay Japan’s capital levy, excess war profits tax and increased property tax. The United States favors national treatment except for the capital levy, while British representatives favor broader exemption.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of message on Japanese tax program
subfiles.about: Forwards a Supreme Commander message concerning Japan’s tax program.
subfiles.summary: Transmits the message at the State-War-Navy Coordinating Committee’s request.

subfiles.title: Japanese tax program
subfiles.about: Requests forwarding of a Supreme Commander message to the Far Eastern Commission.
subfiles.summary: Passes along the Joint Chiefs of Staff request for transmission.

subfiles.title: Directive regarding Japanese taxation of aliens
subfiles.about: Requests transmission of the Commission-based directive to General MacArthur.
subfiles.summary: Asks for review and transmission, including notice that further extraordinary tax policy is under consideration.

subfiles.title: Directive regarding Japanese taxation of aliens
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Sets out instructions based on the Commission’s July 18 policy.
subfiles.summary: Directs nondiscriminatory taxation and capital levy exemptions for United Nations nationals.

subfiles.title: Consultation on extraordinary taxation in Japan
subfiles.about: Reports MacArthur’s objection to immediate publicity about foreign nationals’ tax treatment.
subfiles.summary: The Supreme Commander recommends delaying a press release until the Japanese Diet has acted on the tax bills.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Supreme Commander’s tax publicity recommendation
subfiles.about: Conveys the recommendation to postpone publicity on Japanese extraordinary taxes.
subfiles.summary: Forwards MacArthur’s view that publicity before legislative action would hamper the tax program.

subfiles.title: Routing note for Far Eastern Commission correspondence
subfiles.about: Requests routing of the attached correspondence for action.
subfiles.summary: Directs the letter to the appropriate division.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Commission decision to defer tax press release
subfiles.about: Reports agreement to postpone a press release until Japan’s Diet finishes the tax bills.
subfiles.summary: Johnson asks that the Supreme Commander be informed of the Commission’s unanimous decision.

subfiles.title: Views on releasing Japanese tax consultations to the press
subfiles.about: Requests notice to SCAP that the Commission accepted postponement.
subfiles.summary: Asks that SCAP be told the Commission will wait for Diet action before releasing its consultations.

subfiles.title: Application of capital levy to Koreans resident in Japan
subfiles.from: Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs
subfiles.about: Raises the unsettled question of applying Japan’s capital levy to Korean residents.
subfiles.summary: Reviews Korean assets, repatriation and possible use of Korean ownership to conceal Japanese property, and proposes interdivisional discussion.

subfiles.title: Telegram on capital levy for Koreans in Japan
subfiles.to: Political Adviser, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Requests discussion of whether the capital levy should apply to Koreans in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Suggests considering exemption for Koreans intending to return to Korea, while noting implications for Formosans and concealed Japanese ownership.

subfiles.title: Korean objections to the property tax
subfiles.about: Argues that Koreans should not bear a Japanese tax associated with war costs.
subfiles.summary: The surviving page rejects treating Koreans as Japanese and invokes the Potsdam Declaration and Japan’s colonial rule.

subfiles.title: Tokyo telegram on Korean and Formosan capital levy exemptions
subfiles.about: Explains current exemption policy and its implications for Koreans and Formosans.
subfiles.summary: Reports that Commission policy exempts only United Nations nationals; roughly 20,000 Koreans may face the levy. Requests SCAP consultation before any United States proposal to change policy.

subfiles.title: Routing memorandum on Swiss Legation request
subfiles.to: Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs
subfiles.about: Forwards the Swiss Legation’s memorandum for action.
subfiles.summary: Requests consultation with concerned divisions and notice of the reply.

subfiles.title: Swiss request for equal treatment under Japanese tax laws
subfiles.about: Seeks tax exemptions for Swiss nationals and firms comparable to those of Allied nationals.
subfiles.summary: The Legation invokes the 1911 Swiss-Japanese Treaty’s most-favored-nation clause and Switzerland’s wartime protecting-power role. It asks the United States to seek revision of the exclusion of Swiss property from capital levy and war indemnity exemptions.

subfiles.title: Reply to Swiss Legation on Japanese extraordinary taxes
subfiles.about: Explains the United States response to Switzerland’s tax exemption request.
subfiles.summary: The damaged text traces the United Nations property exemption to Far Eastern Commission policy and says the Swiss memorandum and reply will be referred to the Commission. It also addresses property taken during the war.

subfiles.title: Application of Japanese extraordinary taxes to Swiss property
subfiles.to: United States Representative, Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.about: Forwards the Swiss request and State Department reply to the Commission.
subfiles.summary: Invites Commission comments or other action on Swiss property taxation.

subfiles.title: Transmittal slip for Swiss tax correspondence
subfiles.about: Routes copies of the Swiss correspondence and Far Eastern Commission material.
subfiles.summary: Contains routing instructions for the attached documents.

subfiles.title: Letter forwarding Swiss tax request to Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.about: Sends the Swiss memorandum and State Department reply for Commission consideration.
subfiles.summary: Requests such action as the Commission desires on Swiss property taxation.

subfiles.title: Recommendation on Swiss extraordinary tax request
subfiles.about: Recommends referring the Swiss request and State reply to the Far Eastern Commission.
subfiles.summary: Summarizes how United States and Commission positions on taxing United Nations property developed in 1946.

subfiles.title: Swiss request for equal treatment under Japanese tax laws
subfiles.about: Repeats the Swiss request for exemptions equal to those granted Allied nationals.
subfiles.summary: Cites the 1911 treaty’s most-favored-nation provision and Switzerland’s protecting-power service, and asks the United States to seek revision of the tax policy.

subfiles.title: British proposal for protection against Japanese war-cost taxes
subfiles.about: Proposes wording to exempt United Nations nationals from Japanese war-cost and discriminatory taxes.
subfiles.summary: Everson submits a British draft clause for a proposed Far Eastern Commission paper on United Nations property in Japan.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of British tax clause proposal
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the proposed clause on United Nations property in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Says the suggestion has been passed to those drafting the paper.

subfiles.title: Response to British proposal on extraordinary taxes
subfiles.about: Offers tentative comments on the British tax exemption wording.
subfiles.summary: Martin discusses how the proposed exemption fits the developing United Nations property paper and related tax policy.

subfiles.title: Routing note on Far Eastern Commission’s Swiss decision
subfiles.about: Routes General McCoy’s letter on Switzerland’s tax request.
subfiles.summary: Suggests informing the Swiss desk for communication to the Legation.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Commission decision on Swiss tax exemptions
subfiles.about: Reports the Commission’s refusal to exempt Swiss property from Japanese extraordinary taxes.
subfiles.summary: The Commission says neutral nationals benefited from wartime business in Japan and should remain subject to local taxes. It declines to interpret the 1911 Swiss-Japanese treaty.

subfiles.title: State Department reply conveying Swiss tax decision
subfiles.about: Conveys the Far Eastern Commission’s response to the Swiss exemption request.
subfiles.summary: Quotes the Commission’s refusal and its view that neutral-country nationals remain subject to Japanese taxation. The Commission leaves treaty interpretation outside its remit.

subfiles.title: Record-copy replacement notice for Tokyo despatch 91
subfiles.about: Designates a copy of Tokyo despatch 91 as the record copy.
subfiles.summary: Replaces an original action copy that was not returned to central records.

subfiles.title: Despatch 91: Japanese tax reform discussion
subfiles.about: Transmits a report on a Tokyo discussion of Japanese tax reform.
subfiles.summary: Sebald highlights widespread delinquency, inflationary deficit spending, high corporate taxes and employers’ misuse of withheld taxes. He also encloses a press release on action against delinquent corporations.

subfiles.title: Report on Economic Study Council discussion of Japanese tax reform
subfiles.from: Office of the United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Records a Tokyo meeting on tax reform, collection and Japanese government finance.
subfiles.summary: Speakers review the 1947 tax reforms, self-assessment and large arrears. They dispute corporate tax rates, collectors’ discretion, underfunded collection offices and employers’ retention of withheld taxes. The discussion also covers deficit finance, local taxes and difficulties collecting from Chinese and Korean residents.

subfiles.title: Despatch 91: Japanese tax reform discussion
subfiles.about: Repeats the despatch transmitting the Economic Study Council report.
subfiles.summary: Summarizes delinquent payments, deficit finance, corporate tax rates and misappropriated withholding taxes.

subfiles.title: Report on Economic Study Council discussion of Japanese tax reform
subfiles.from: Office of the United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Repeats the meeting report; its text continues beyond this section.
subfiles.summary: The report reviews the 1947 reforms and disputes over tax rates, self-assessment, delinquency, collectors’ conduct and corporate withholding arrears. Speakers link weak collection to deficit finance and discuss the difficulty of taxing Chinese and Korean residents. Page 68 ends during the repeated account of that discussion.
